retryPolicy: Product checks never retry. An infrastructure failure may rerun the entire job in a clean environment with both attempts retained.

gates.name: core-matrix
gates.reason: Stable and Rust 1.89 format, lint, unit, integration, and schema checks run on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

gates.name: package-install
gates.reason: Cargo packaging and locked source installation run on Linux.

gates.name: dependency-review
gates.reason: RustSec, crates.io source, and reviewed-license checks run for all release targets.

gates.name: release-archives
gates.reason: Native archives and the standalone companion-skill ZIP have deterministic manifests, digests, checksums, and verification.

gates.name: deterministic-fake-server
gates.reason: The feature-gated independent fixture covers fragmented and invalid frames, delayed and out-of-order IDs, diagnostics, progress, callbacks, crash, and hang scenarios.

gates.name: reference-server-smoke
gates.reason: Nightly and candidate matrices run exact recorded rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server, TypeScript, Node, basedpyright, and Python versions on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

gates.name: native-floor-acceptance
gates.reason: Linux artifacts build and smoke in native manylinux 2.28 containers; self-hosted Intel/ARM macOS 12 and Windows Server 2019 floor runners smoke extracted archives, while every artifact also receives a static floor audit.

gates.name: stored-state-compatibility
gates.reason: The immutable 1.0.0 first-release seed covers Trust, Denial, Preview, Receipt, and Recovery records; digest and Rust deserialization checks run in CI.

gates.name: performance-and-soak
gates.reason: Nightly and candidate matrices enforce cold readiness, 100-query warm p95, 1,000 operations, process/handle/memory bounds, and Document and diagnostic churn on every OS.
